Design

Source: DESIGN.md

misocialr reproduces the architecture of ibger for a different source: the MDS MI Social API, an open Apache Solr select handler with one document per municipality x month (codigo_ibge, 6 digits; anomes_s, YYYYMM).

Component File Responsibility
HTTP core R/utils.R mds_request() (httr2, retries on 5xx/429 only, Solr error message surfaced), Solr filter builders
Dictionary R/fields.R, inst/extdata/*.csv Curated fields per theme; mds_api_fields() scans the live schema
Localities R/localidades.R Locality parsing, ibge_code7() (check digit + 9 exceptions), mds_localities()
Periods R/periodos.R Period parsing, mds_periods() via Solr facets (all values vs non-zero)
Retrieval R/dados.R Query plan (states + municipality chunks of 200), Solr paging (10,000 rows), long output
Validation + cache R/validacao.R Field checks, session cache, mds_clear_cache()
Publication rule R/publicacao.R mds_drop_unpublished()

Decisions that differ from ibger, and why:

  • value is numeric. IBGE encodes missingness in special strings, so ibger keeps value as character. MI Social returns JSON numbers and encodes absence by leaving the field out of the document, so absent fields simply produce no row.
  • Zeros are not always zeros. The API returns 0 for months not yet published. Rather than silently dropping them, mds_data() returns what was published and mds_drop_unpublished() applies the rule explicitly (same rule as the BDE collector etl/fontes/coletores/mds.R).
  • Field validation asks for data, not schema. The Solr schema has dynamic fields (*_i, *_f, …), so any suffixed name is “defined”. A field is accepted when at least one document has it (numFound > 0).
  • The server labels JSON as text/plain, so responses are parsed with check_type = FALSE.
  • Labels are in Portuguese, as the source; the dictionary lives in CSV so that R code stays ASCII and the Python sibling reads the same file.
  • Fail loudly on inputs that would widen or narrow the query. An empty locality vector would mean “no filter”, i.e. the whole country; a wrong check digit would silently become another municipality. Both are errors (0.2.1), as are text fields, whose values would otherwise become NA and vanish from the long output.
  • An empty page is not the end. Paging stops only when numFound is reached; an empty page before that, Solr’s partialResults or a response without response is an error.
  • Unpublished months can be judged by the whole country. mds_drop_unpublished(reference = "brazil") reads the last month with a non-zero value from mds_periods(), so a small selection keeps its legitimate trailing zeros.
  • One response contract, checked before anything else (0.3.0). Data pages, counts and facets go through check_response() (R/resposta.R) before they are interpreted or cached; then every document must carry a valid municipality and month and at most one value per field. A failure of the source can therefore never become “no data” for the rest of the session, nor shift a value to another municipality.
  • Repetition is fine, contradiction is not. Observations repeated with the same value are dropped; different values for the same key are a misocialr_error_conflict.
  • Classification before deletion. mds_drop_unpublished() never removes a non-zero value, re-reads a contradictory national reference, and can only flag (action = "flag"), because inferring publication from zeros is a heuristic, not an official date.
  • POST, not GET (0.3.1). The Solr select handler answers a form POST exactly like a GET, and a long GET URL is refused with HTTP 414 (measured at about 8,000 characters). Municipality codes are still split in blocks of 200 to keep each filter small.
  • Retries are tested against a real server. httr2’s mocked responses and Python’s responses return before the retry loop, so the retry tests use a local HTTP server (webfakes in R, http.server in Python). Both packages make 3 tries in total.
  • Behaviour parity is tested, not assumed. tests/testthat/paridade/ casos.json lists inputs and expected outputs or error classes; both test suites run it (the Python copy is kept by sincronizar_python.py).
  • Paging with cursorMark (0.4.0). Pages are walked by the sort key (id), so documents added or removed while reading cannot shift them; a changing total and repeated ids are still errors, and reading stops at numFound without an extra request.
  • Nature with its basis (0.4.0). Each field says how it may be summed and whether that was measured on the monthly series or inferred. An inferred nature is a default to check, not a fact.

Developed by André Leite, Marcos Wasiliew, Hugo Vasconcelos, Carlos Amorim, Diogo Bezerra, Júlia Nascimento Barreto.
